slot.brief: Prism / mirror combination: two thin prisms in contact giving deviation without dispersion; use ω and net deviation conditions, or solve two equations in two unknowns for the prism angles.

stem: Two thin prisms are placed in opposite orientations. Their refractive indices are $1.5$ and $1.6$, and their dispersive powers are $0.04$ and $0.06$, respectively. If the first prism has angle $6^\circ$, the combination produces no dispersion. Find the second prism's angle and the net mean deviation.

verdicts.working: No dispersion requires 0.04(1.5−1)(6°)=0.06(1.6−1)A₂, giving A₂=10/3°. The opposing mean deviations are 3° and 2°, so the net is 1°.

working:
No dispersion: $0.04(1.5-1)(6^\circ)=0.06(1.6-1)A_2$\\
$A_2=\dfrac{10}{3}^\circ$\\
$\delta_1=(1.5-1)(6^\circ)=3^\circ$; $\delta_2=(1.6-1)\dfrac{10}{3}^\circ=2^\circ$\\
$\delta_{\rm net}=\delta_1-\delta_2=1^\circ$

Independent check: No dispersion requires 0.04(1.5−1)(6°)=0.06(1.6−1)A₂, giving A₂=10/3°. The opposing mean deviations are 3° and 2°, so the net is 1°.
solution: For no dispersion, the dispersive deviations must cancel: $\omega_1(\mu_1-1)A_1=\omega_2(\mu_2-1)A_2$, giving $A_2=\dfrac{0.04(0.5)(6^\circ)}{0.06(0.6)}=\dfrac{10}{3}^\circ$$.\nThe$ mean deviations oppose: $\delta_{\rm net}=(1.5-1)(6^\circ)-(1.6-1)\left(\dfrac{10}{3}^\circ\right)=3^\circ-2^\circ=1^\circ$.
